text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- FUND MANAGER SUSPENDED IN POACHING ROW

One of the most powerful fund managers in the City of London has been suspended amid allegations she tried to lure about 20 colleagues at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell to move with her to another bank. Nicola Horlick has been suspended by Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, which is owned by Germany's Deutsche Bank, "pending an internal investigation into what we think might be a breach of her contract", said MGAM chief executive Robert Smith. The incident comes as a blow to MGAM following the recent high profile deception case involving another fund manager, Peter Young.
-- BRUSSELS 'WARNED BA' OVER AMERICAN ALLIANCE

Karel van Miert, the European competition commissioner, has said that European Union members have been repeatedly warned not to wave through transatlantic airline alliances without referring to Brussels. The comments come as the Commission is locked in a dispute with the British government over the proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines. Van Miert has threatened legal action against the UK if it approves the alliance, which rival airlines claim will be anti-competitive.
-- MPS URGE CLARKE TO AGREE INTEREST RATE RISE

A report from the all-party Treasury select committee has urged chancellor Kenneth Clarke to raise interest rates in order to avoid stimulating inflation. The report also questioned the realism of the tax and public spending plans announced in the November Budget. The call to increase interest rates is likely to be echoed by Eddie George, governor of the Bank of England, when he meets the chancellor in their monthly meeting due on Wednesday.
-- FINANCIAL BRANDS 'FAIL TO CATCH ON'

A review of the financial services industry has found that companies in the sector have failed to build up any significant value for their brand names. The research, from stockbroker Dresdner Kleinwort Benson and the brand strategy consultants Interbrand, found that only Barclaycard had succeeded in building up brand name value. The study claimed that the Barclaycard brand is worth 1.33 billion stg, 5.4 times its 1995 profits. Barclaycard is the credit card arm of Barclays Bank.
-- AIRCRAFT TAX CHANGE MAY BE RECONSIDERED

William Waldegrave, the chief Treasury secretary, has told the Commons that the airline industry had a legitimate point with its objections to a reduction in capital allowances for aircraft which was announced in the November Budget. Waldegrave added that the issue would certainly be discussed further. However, the comments were later played down by officials, who said the aircraft industry had no better case than did ships or trains.
-- TOUGHER CURBS URGED ON PRIVATIZED UTILITIES

An independent cross-party body has said that curbs on anti- competitive behaviour, including fines for predatory commercial practices, are needed in the privatized utilities. The Commission on the Regulation of the Privatized Utilities also proposed clarifying the role of regulators, increasing the representation of consumers in regulation, and the eventual replacement of single-person regulators with executive boards. In a wide-ranging review, the Commission warned that public confidence in regulation cannot be enhanced without greater transparency and accountability.
-- CHIEF EXECUTIVE LEAVES NATIONAL EXPRESS GROUP

Ernest Patterson, chief executive of National Express group, has left the company "by mutual agreement" after just six months at the helm. Patterson, who joined the coach, bus and rail operator on a one-year contract from BET, the business services group, is understood to be expecting a pay-off of about 250,000 pounds stg. Colin Child, finance director of National Express, said of the decision: "it was mutually agreed that he was not right for us and we were not right for him".
-- VALUE OF RUMP HANSON GROUP PUT AT 2.3 BILLION STG

Broker ABN Amro Hoare Govett has said that Hanson is likely to command a stock market value of 2.3 billion pounds stg following the demerger of its energy business next month. The energy business, known as Energy Group, comprises UK regional electricity group Eastern Electricity, and Peabody, the biggest coal miner in the US. The demerger will complete the break-up of the Hanson conglomerate, which will be left simply as a building materials producer.
-- CERNON TO JOIN C&W MOBILE

Cable & Wireless has appointed Lisa Gernon, formerly director of strategy and marketing for mobile phone operator Orange, as regional director of its mobile phone business in Europe. Gernon has been widely identified with Orange's distinctive marketing campaign, which has been credited as a major factor in the rapid growth of Orange to take second place in the UK mobile phone market.
-- MATTHEW CLARK TO REFRESH CIDER BRANDS

Drinks producer Matthew Clark has unveiled plans for rebuilding its battered Dry Blackthorn and Diamond White cider brands. The group has been under pressure from new brands, and has seen its shares halved since September. Management pointed to three main reasons for the poor performance: the collapse in volume and profits of Diamond White, lower prices in the trade- off for all its ciders, and a loss of share for Dry Blackthorn because of its dated image.
